packet.description_seed: According to Bloomberg, OpenAI has enlisted an outside law firm to work through its options.

what: OpenAI is reportedly preparing legal action against Apple; it wouldn’t be the first partner to feel burned

clean_source_blocks.text: OpenAI is so frustrated with Apple over a ChatGPT integration that failed to deliver the subscribers and prominence it expected that the company is now actively exploring legal action against the iPhone maker, Bloomberg News reported Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter. According to Bloomberg, OpenAI has enlisted an outside law firm to work through its options, which could include sending Apple a formal breach-of-contract notice without necessarily escalating to a full lawsuit (at least not immediately). Any legal move would likely wait until after the conclusion of OpenAI’s ongoing trial with Elon Musk. ---

Apple and OpenAI inked a deal to integrate ChatGPT with Siri as part of iOS 18 in 2024. According to a new report today, however, OpenAI is displeased with how the partnership has played out and is considering taking legal action against Apple. According to Bloomberg, OpenAI lawyers are working with an outside legal firm “on a range of options that could be formally executed in the near future.” One possible outcome is that OpenAI sends Apple a notice “alleging breach of contract without necessarily filing a full lawsuit at the outset.” “OpenAI believed that the companies’ partnership, which wove ChatGPT into Apple software, would coax more users into subscribing to the chatbot. It also expected deeper integration across more Apple apps and prime placement within the Siri assistant.”
According to Bloomberg, OpenAI has enlisted an outside law firm to work through its options.

OpenAI is preparing to potentially take legal action against Apple due to a "strained" relationship with the iPhone maker, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. The two companies reached a partnership in 2024 that saw ChatGPT integrated into features like Siri and Image Playground across iOS, iPadOS, and macOS. iPhone users can also subscribe to ChatGPT directly via the Settings app, with Apple taking a cut of revenue. Ultimately, though, the report said OpenAI expected ChatGPT to be more deeply integrated across additional Apple apps and to have more prime placement within Siri. OpenAI executives also believe that Apple has not sufficiently advertised the integration, resulting in fewer customers knowing about it.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: TechCrunch]
OpenAI is so frustrated with Apple over a ChatGPT integration that failed to deliver the subscribers and prominence it expected that the company is now actively exploring legal action against the iPhone maker, Bloomberg News reported Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.

According to Bloomberg, OpenAI has enlisted an outside law firm to work through its options, which could include sending Apple a formal breach-of-contract notice without necessarily escalating to a full lawsuit (at least not immediately). Any legal move would likely wait until after the conclusion of OpenAI’s ongoing trial with Elon Musk.

---

[Lähde: 9to5Mac]
Apple and OpenAI inked a deal to integrate ChatGPT with Siri as part of iOS 18 in 2024. According to a new report today, however, OpenAI is displeased with how the partnership has played out and is considering taking legal action against Apple.

According to Bloomberg, OpenAI lawyers are working with an outside legal firm “on a range of options that could be formally executed in the near future.” One possible outcome is that OpenAI sends Apple a notice “alleging breach of contract without necessarily filing a full lawsuit at the outset.”

“OpenAI believed that the companies’ partnership, which wove ChatGPT into Apple software, would coax more users into subscribing to the chatbot. It also expected deeper integration across more Apple apps and prime placement within the Siri assistant.”

An unnamed OpenAI executive, quoted by Bloomberg, alleges that the company has “done everything from a product perspective,” while Apple has not held up its end of the deal.

“We have done everything from a product perspective,” the executive said. “They have not, and worse, they haven’t even made an honest effort.”

One aspect of the OpenAI integration into iOS is the ability to sign up for a paid ChatGPT subscription via the Settings app on iPhone. OpenAI reportedly believed this “could generate billions of dollars per year in subscriptions,” which apparently “hasn’t come close to happening.”

“When we heard about this opportunity, it sounded amazing: being able to acquire a giant number of customers and have distribution in such a big mobile ecosystem,” said the OpenAI executive. At the time, though, Apple was unwilling to share exactly what the product would be, the person said.

“They basically said, ‘OpenAI needs to take a leap of faith and trust us,’” the executive said, adding that the deal ended up being a failure for the startup.

There is no money changing hands between Apple and OpenAI as part of this deal, outside of Apple getting a cut of those subscriptions. Apple is not paying OpenAI for use of its technology.

OpenAI’s displeasure comes ahead of WWDC, where Apple is expected to announce a next-generation version of Siri powered by Google Gemini. iOS 27 will also reportedly let users integrate with other AI models, including Anthropic’s Claude.

Apple opening the iPhone up to other AI models “isn’t driving the company’s legal action since the partnership wasn’t meant to be exclusive from the start,” according to the unnamed OpenAI executive.

Ultimately, though, the report said OpenAI expected ChatGPT to be more deeply integrated across additional Apple apps and to have more prime placement within Siri.

OpenAI executives also believe that Apple has not sufficiently advertised the integration, resulting in fewer customers knowing about it.

Apple's culture of secrecy is said to have resulted in OpenAI not knowing exactly how ChatGPT would be integrated on the iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

payload.title: OpenAI harkitsee oikeustoimia Applea vastaan ChatGPT-yhteistyön vuoksi
payload.summary: OpenAI on raporttien mukaan turhautunut siihen, miten sen ChatGPT-yhteistyö Applen kanssa on toteutunut, ja selvittää nyt mahdollisia oikeudellisia toimia.
payload.content:
OpenAI selvittää mahdollisia oikeudellisia toimia Applea vastaan, koska yhtiö on raporttien mukaan pettynyt ChatGPT-integraation näkyvyyteen ja kaupallisiin tuloksiin Applen laitteissa. Bloombergin tietoihin viittaavien raporttien mukaan OpenAI on ottanut ulkopuolisen lakitoimiston avukseen arvioidakseen vaihtoehtojaan, joihin voisi kuulua sopimusrikkomusta koskeva virallinen ilmoitus ilman välitöntä täysimittaista oikeusjuttua.

## Kiista liittyy ChatGPT:n näkyvyyteen Applen ohjelmistoissa

Apple ja OpenAI sopivat vuonna 2024 ChatGPT:n tuomisesta osaksi Applen ohjelmistoja. Yhteistyö näkyi muun muassa Sirin yhteydessä sekä Applen käyttöjärjestelmissä, kuten iOS:ssä, iPadOS:ssä ja macOS:ssä. Käyttäjät ovat voineet hyödyntää ChatGPT:tä tietyissä Applen toiminnoissa, ja iPhonen käyttäjille on tarjottu mahdollisuus tilata ChatGPT suoraan asetusten kautta.

Raporttien mukaan OpenAI odotti kumppanuudelta enemmän. Yhtiön kerrotaan uskoneen, että ChatGPT saisi vahvemman aseman Sirissä, laajemman integraation Applen sovelluksiin ja paremman näkyvyyden käyttäjille. OpenAI:n johdon kerrotaan myös arvioivan, ettei Apple ole tuonut integraatiota esiin riittävästi, mikä olisi osaltaan vähentänyt käyttäjien tietoisuutta palvelusta.

## Mahdollinen oikeudellinen askel ei välttämättä tarkoittaisi heti oikeusjuttua

Tällä hetkellä kyse on raporttien mukaan vaihtoehtojen selvittämisestä, ei vahvistetusta oikeudenkäynnistä. Yksi mahdollinen askel olisi muodollinen ilmoitus, jossa OpenAI väittäisi Applen rikkoneen sopimusta. Sellainen ilmoitus voisi avata tien neuvotteluille tai myöhemmille oikeudellisille toimille, mutta se ei automaattisesti merkitsisi kanteen nostamista.

Raporttien mukaan mahdollinen eteneminen saattaa myös ajoittua vasta OpenAI:n ja Elon Muskin välisen oikeusprosessin jälkeen. Tämä viittaa siihen, että yhtiö punnitsee etenemistään varovasti eikä välttämättä halua avata uutta suurta oikeudellista rintamaa heti.

Tapaus korostaa, kuinka herkkä suurten teknologiayhtiöiden välinen tekoälykumppanuus voi olla, kun odotukset näkyvyydestä, käyttäjämääristä ja tilaustuloista eivät kohtaa. Applelle ChatGPT-integraatio on ollut osa laajempaa pyrkimystä tuoda generatiivista tekoälyä sen ekosysteemiin, kun taas OpenAI:lle Applen laite- ja käyttäjäkunta on potentiaalisesti tärkeä kasvukanava.
summary_bullets: OpenAI selvittää raporttien mukaan oikeudellisia vaihtoehtoja Applea vastaan.
Kiista liittyy ChatGPT-integraation näkyvyyteen, laajuuteen ja odotettuihin tilaajamääriin.
Mahdollinen ensimmäinen askel voisi olla sopimusrikkomusta koskeva virallinen ilmoitus, ei välttämättä heti oikeusjuttu.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu annettuun monilähteiseen pakettiin, jossa keskeinen tieto nojaa Bloombergin raportointiin TechCrunchin, 9to5Macin ja MacRumorsin välittämänä. Väitteet on muotoiltu raportoiduiksi, koska OpenAI:n tai Applen virallista vahvistusta ei paketissa ollut.

The two companies reached a partnership in 2024 that saw ChatGPT integrated into features like Siri and Image Playground across iOS, iPadOS, and macOS. iPhone users can also subscribe to ChatGPT directly via the Settings app, with Apple taking a cut of revenue. Ultimately, though, the report said OpenAI expected ChatGPT to be more deeply integrated across additional Apple apps and to have more prime placement within Siri. OpenAI executives also believe that Apple has not sufficiently advertised the integration, resulting in fewer customers knowing about it.
